key_insight: Dead-end pores are not just inactive voids: their density and placement along flow paths can increase intrinsic permeability through local hydrodynamic interactions at junctions.
engineering_relevance: Permeability models for porous media should account for dead-end pore architecture, not only porosity and pore-size statistics, to better predict transport in natural and engineered materials.
method: Performed pore-scale flow simulations on heterogeneous dead-end pore arrangements.
Compared controlled granular assemblies with a minimal single-channel model.
Isolated effects of dead-end pore density, depth, and orientation while preserving the transmitting network.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based comparisons showing permeability enhancement with higher dead-end pore density along percolating paths, while pore depth and junction orientation showed negligible effects.
watch_item: The proposed effective formulation is inferred from pore-scale simulations, so validation on experimental porous media and broader geometries is still needed.
paper_title: Pore-shape and its spatial organization control intrinsic permeability of porous media
